77. Deputy Rose Conway-Walsh asked the Minister for Enterprise, Tourism and Employment to report on the measurable improvements in collective bargaining coverage in Ireland in the year since the publication of the Government’s action plan to promote collective bargaining. [79772/26]

78. Deputy Brian Stanley asked the Minister for Enterprise, Tourism and Employment for a progress report on land owned by the IDA outside of Portlaoise; when funding will be allocated for it; and the plans to develop the site. [79467/26]

79. Deputy Rose Conway-Walsh asked the Minister for Enterprise, Tourism and Employment the reason for not waiting for the Oireachtas Joint Committee on Enterprise, Tourism and Employment to finish its pre-legislative scrutiny of the Short-Term Letting and Tourism Bill 2026 and to publish its PLS report, with its recommendations, before the final Bill was introduced. [79774/26]

80. Deputy Rose Conway-Walsh asked the Minister for Enterprise, Tourism and Employment in light of his proposal to cap minor injury payouts, the action that will be taken to ensure the savings being made by insurance companies from reduced claims will be passed on to business owners to reduce the cost of doing business. [79456/26]

81. Deputy James Geoghegan asked the Minister for Enterprise, Tourism and Employment if he will provide an overview of the Startup Ireland programme; and to provide a breakdown of the funding associated with it. [79506/26]

82. Deputy Martin Daly asked the Minister for Enterprise, Tourism and Employment the specific measures he intends to introduce to address persistently high commercial vacancy rates in rural towns, particularly Boyle, County Roscommon, where the commercial vacancy rate has reached 30.1%, and Ballinasloe, County Galway; whether targeted financial supports, enterprise incentives or retail activation schemes will be introduced to encourage businesses to occupy vacant commercial premises in these towns; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [79458/26]

83. Deputy George Lawlor asked the Minister for Enterprise, Tourism and Employment given the role social enterprises play in sustaining employment and services in towns and villages where private sector investment may be limited, if he will introduce targeted grants or tax incentives for social enterprises operating in rural and disadvantaged areas. [79464/26]

84. Deputy Emer Currie asked the Minister for Enterprise, Tourism and Employment the timeline for the development and publication of the Enterprise 2035 Strategy; the plans for further consultation with businesses; and the way in which key enterprise sectors falling under the remit of other Government Departments will be incorporated into the strategy. [79393/26]
86. Deputy Aisling Dempsey asked the Minister for Enterprise, Tourism and Employment for an overview of the Startup Ireland initiative. [79289/26]

87. Deputy Colm Burke asked the Minister for Enterprise, Tourism and Employment to provide an update on his Department's progress in establishing a single application process for employment permits and visa applications. [79274/26]
88. Deputy John Connolly asked the Minister for Enterprise, Tourism and Employment when a new western regional enterprise plan will be brought forward. [79402/26]

91. Deputy Naoise Ó Cearúil asked the Minister for Enterprise, Tourism and Employment the specific artificial intelligence technologies and research areas that Ireland intends to prioritise under the Important Project of Common European Interest (IPCEI) in Artificial Intelligence (AI); and the way in which these priorities will be determined. [79389/26]

95. Deputy Colm Burke asked the Minister for Enterprise, Tourism and Employment the current status of the Pregnancy Loss (Miscellaneous Provisions) Bill 2025; and the changes that are envisaged. [79272/26]
